source: make a game that has a beautiful map with a lobby before the match starts, players spawn in the lobby and once the match starts once another match is finished and. players then spawn into a beautiful arena arcade themed where players have to do mini games and get more points per mini game they finish, whoever has the most points wins the round a d gets awarded some coins which they can use at the shop in the lobby where they can buy auras

image_prompt.text: A beautiful lobby where the whole server spawns and waits between matches, sized so nobody bottlenecks at the exits
A prominent wall in the lobby sized to host the round's point standings
An out-of-play area where players who have finished a mini-game can wait and watch
The markers that move everyone from the lobby into the arcade arena and back at round end
A vibrant arcade-themed arena holding several distinct mini-game areas
A shop counter in the lobby where players spend coins on auras

layout_placement.text: Detection regions in each mini-game area that register a completion and award points
The point standings surface, updated as players finish mini-games
Lobby-to-arena and arena-to-lobby transport markers fired at round start and end
Spawn points in the lobby for arriving players, and evenly distributed start points in the arena

notes: Lobby and arena are separated per the staged shape, which is P4 - two maps generated separately.

The mini-games themselves have no option: the arena is emitted as one arcade space with several sub-areas rather than as N authored stations, because neither the count nor the kind of mini-game was given.
Coins, points, the shop and the aura purchases are economy, not layout. Only the shop's physical counter survives into the build.

open_questions.ask: How many mini-games, and what are they? Their kind decides the arena's internal layout.
How many players per round - it sets the size of both the lobby and the arena.

theme: Arcade - bright neon, colourful and stylized

coverage_missing.ask: Should the lobby share the arcade look, or contrast with it?

answers.ask: How many mini-games, and what are they? Their kind decides the arena's internal layout.
answers.answer: Use three simple arcade-themed mini-games: a coin-collecting race, an obstacle-course race, and a target-hitting game. Each should be a quick round where finishing or performing well awards points.

answers.ask: How many players per round - it sets the size of both the lobby and the arena.
answers.answer: Support up to 8 players per round, keeping the lobby and arcade arena compact but comfortable.
